seo.title: Child destiny matrix: how to read your child's chart
seo.description: Child destiny matrix means two charts: your child's personal matrix from one date and parent–child compatibility from two. Which to use and where to start.

title: Your child's destiny matrix: a personal chart and a parent–child chart
short: A child destiny matrix is not a special children's calculation but two different ways of looking at a child. Your child's personal matrix is built from their date of birth alone and describes the child: their character, their talents, what is worth supporting. The parent–child compatibility matrix is built from two dates and describes the relationship: how you get on, where you clash, which approach suits the child best. Choose by your question: if it is about the child, you need the personal matrix; if it is "how do I deal with them?", you need compatibility. In both cases the numbers come from the same engine used for adults. What changes is not the formula but how you read the result for a child's age.

sections.h2: Two child matrices: which one you need

head: Your child's personal matrix
Parent–child compatibility
rows: two — the parent's and the child's
character, talents, where the child feels at ease, what to support
the relationship: approach, conflicts, where you are alike and where you differ
"What are they like? What comes easily to them? What fills them up?"
"How do I handle them? Why do we argue? How do I reach them?"
the usual matrix diagram for their date
a third matrix, shared by the two of you

paragraphs: **The personal matrix** describes the child on their own, without you. It is useful when you want to understand better what suits them, what they rely on and where they need support.

**Compatibility** describes neither the child nor you, but what happens between you. It is the one to look at when the question is about the relationship: you love each other but can't seem to agree, or everything goes smoothly with one child and every day is a battle with another.

There is a third thing that often goes by a similar name: the parent-child line. These are three points inside any personal matrix: the childhood home, the attitude to children, and how that experience comes out into the world. Everyone has one, including adults without children, and it describes one person, not a parent–child pair. It is covered in detail in a separate article on the parent-child line.

sections.h2: How to get your child's personal matrix
paragraphs: Enter your child's date of birth into the calculation form, just as you would your own: it is the ordinary matrix calculation. You don't need the time or place of birth, and sex does not affect the numbers. You will get the same diagram as for an adult: the eight-pointed star of arcana, the chakra table and the sections of the reading.

The site has no special children's report, and we won't pass off an adult text as a children's one. A child's numbers are the same as anyone's with that date, while the texts of the automatic reading are written for an adult reader. So read them as a description of energies that are still taking shape in the child, and translate them into the language of their age — how to do that is explained below.
Let's calculate a worked example — 12 April 2016:
There is one rule: if a sum is greater than 22, add its digits; 22 stays as it is. The portrait 12 is The Hanged Man, and the centre 5 is The Hierophant.

sections.h2: Where to start reading: portrait, centre and talents
paragraphs: The full reading order is the same for everyone and is set out in the general guide. With a child's chart it is easier to start from three places — they depend least on adult experience.

head: What to look at
Where on the diagram
What it's about
A question for your own observations
rows: A, the left corner, the day of birth
how others see the child and how they get to know the world
How do their teacher, nursery carer or grandmother — people who see them from the outside — describe them?
E, the middle of the star
where they feel at ease and what restores them
After what do they recover fastest?
the line B → P → K, from the top corner to the centre
what comes easily and what can be developed
What will they do for a long time without being reminded?

paragraphs: Read each of the three places as a question, not an answer. The arcanum names a direction, and your observations confirm it: what the child chooses when nobody is steering them, what they complain about, when they light up.
The date is made up; there is no real child behind it. But the numbers have been checked against the calculator's engine, and you can repeat the observations with your own date.

**Portrait 12 — The Hanged Man.** The child looks at everything from their own angle. They may be slow to answer, not out of stubbornness but because they need to look things over. They often sympathise, give way, and notice the one who has been hurt. Question: when they are hurried, do they cope faster — or get stuck?

**Centre 5 — The Hierophant.** They feel at ease where it is clear how things work and why. A child like this loves explanations, often asks "why?" and trusts an adult who knows what they are doing. Question: does it get easier for them when a rule is explained rather than simply imposed?

**Talents 4-13-9 — The Emperor, Death, The Hermit.** The Emperor at the start of the line is order and taking responsibility for your own things. Death in the middle is finishing, clearing away and starting afresh. The Hermit next to the centre is depth and working on your own. Together they suggest a knack for figuring out, alone and unhurried, how something works and putting it in order. Question: what can they do for hours on their own — building, sorting, taking things apart down to the last screw?

Here the portrait and the centre point the same way: **this child needs time and a clear "why".** Pressure to hurry up is more likely to slow them down than speed them up, while an explanation helps them get moving. This is a hypothesis to test, not a description of a child. The same portrait 12 and the same centre 5 belong to 169 dates since 1900, and very different children stand behind them. If a month of observation doesn't bear the picture out, trust your observations.
The same date has 12-11-17 as its parent-child line — The Hanged Man, Strength and The Star. That text is read in full in the article on the line.

sections.h2: How to take age into account
paragraphs: The same arcanum sounds different in a three-year-old and in a teenager. The energy is the same; what changes is where you can see it.

ul: **Before school — in play.** Watch what the child plays on their own and which role they take with other children. The Empress feeds her dolls and builds a house, The Chariot organises races, The Hermit potters about alone for ages.

**In primary school — in learning and rules.** How they learn, from whom, what they do after lessons, how they react to marks and to unfairness. Here Justice can be heard in "that's not fair!", The Hierophant in an endless stream of "why?".

**In a teenager — in independence and friendship.** At this age the chart is better read together with them, not about them. Their opinion of themselves comes first, yours second. Don't read out an arcanum's negative sides as a verdict: teenagers try labels on very easily.

paragraphs: Money, marriage, intimacy, an adult's life purpose — the automatic reading describes these topics for adults. When you read it about a child, simply set those sections aside: you can't translate them by swapping the word "person" for "child".

Taking age into account is our editorial adaptation, not a law of development. Yuliana Lisovskaya has a separate book, Detskaya Matritsa Sudby (The Children's Destiny Matrix), with its own approach to reading a child's chart and an age boundary of about 14–15. Our site does not reproduce her method as a whole: the numbers come from the same engine, and the reading is adapted to the child's age and the parent's question.

paragraphs: **Not every arcanum can appear at every point.** The centre E is never 1, 2, 15, 17, 19 or 21. Point B holds the month of birth, so it can only be 1–12. The middle and the inner end of the talent line, P and K, are never 1 or 2. The portrait A — the day of birth — can be any of the 22. If your diagram shows an "impossible" number at one of these points, check the calculation: numbers like that come from a calculator with different rules.

sections.h2: Parent–child compatibility: what the second date adds
paragraphs: The compatibility matrix is built following Lisovskaya: the matching points of two personal charts are added together and reduced to 22 or less. The result is a third chart — not yours, not the child's, but shared. Lisovskaya says plainly that such a matrix can be made not only for spouses but also for friends, colleagues and other people.

Take a pair of dates: the parent is born on 05.09.1990, the child on 12.04.2016. The parent's personal centre is 12, the child's is 5. The centre of their shared matrix is 12 + 5 = 17, The Star. The Star never appears in the centre of a personal chart, for any date, but in a matrix of two people it can. This shows clearly that compatibility is a separate chart with its own rules, not the sum of two descriptions.

The free compatibility calculator will build this matrix, but its texts are shared by any two people, and some of them are written about partners. For example, the area called "The couple as parents" is about two adults raising a child together, not about a parent's relationship with a son or daughter. None of the automatic texts takes the roles of parent and child into account.

sections.h2: What a child's destiny matrix won't tell you

ul: **How the child is developing.** The matrix does not assess development, behaviour or wellbeing. If something there worries you, take the question to a teacher or a child psychologist, not to a calculation.
**What they will become.** A profession, the "right" club or a school cannot be determined from a date. The talents in the matrix are directions to try, not a ready-made route.
**What they will grow up to be like.** Hundreds of children share the same calculation and lead very different lives; character takes shape in the family, at school, among friends.
**How to raise them.** The matrix suggests questions for your observations, but it does not prescribe the right way to bring a child up.

paragraphs: The automatic reading is an honest reference guide to the parts of the matrix: the portrait, the centre, the talents, the lines and the chakras are each read separately, in their own text. Connecting these parts with one another, with your child's age and with your family's situation is up to you — and the free calculation and the encyclopedia give you everything you need to start.

ul: **If you want to understand the child** — their character, talents, what to support — calculate the matrix from their date for free and start with the portrait, the centre and the talent line, as in the example above.
**If the question is about your relationship** — how to talk to each other, why you argue, which approach suits them — enter your date and your child's date in the free compatibility calculator.
**If you want both**, look at the two matrices side by side, and read the article on the parent-child line to see which family patterns live in your own chart.

paragraphs: Each arcanum, the centre and the talent line have their own pages in the encyclopedia, so you can explore every part of your child's chart in more depth.

faq.q: How is a child's destiny matrix different from an adult's?
faq.a: The calculation is exactly the same: the numbers come from the same formula. The reading is what differs. In a child the energies are still taking shape, so the chart is read through play, learning and friendship, and adult topics such as money and marriage are set aside. Lisovskaya has a separate book about children with its own emphasis; our site does not reproduce her method.

faq.q: Can I calculate a child's destiny matrix in an ordinary calculator?
faq.a: Yes. Enter the child's date into the ordinary calculation and you will get their personal matrix. The texts of the automatic reading are written for an adult reader, so read them with the child's age in mind.

faq.q: Do I need the time and place of birth?
faq.a: No. The destiny matrix is calculated from the date only: day, month and year. The time and place of birth do not affect the numbers.

faq.q: Do I need the parent's date of birth?
faq.a: Not for the child's personal matrix: their date is enough. The parent's date is needed when the question is about the relationship: then a compatibility matrix is built from the two dates.

faq.q: From what age can I look at a child's matrix?
faq.a: You can calculate it from birth: the date is already there. But with a baby there is little to compare the description with. The chart becomes most useful once the child's character shows in play and contact with others, and with a teenager it is best read together with them.

faq.q: How should I read a teenager's matrix?
faq.a: Together with them, with their opinion first. Show them the portrait, the centre and the talents and ask what they recognise. Don't read out the arcana's negative sides as a verdict: they are possible difficulties, not an assessment of character.

faq.q: What if the description doesn't match my child?
faq.a: Trust your observations. An arcanum gives a direction, not a ready-made description: hundreds of different children share the same calculation. If nothing is borne out after a few weeks, put that part of the chart aside and look at the others.

faq.q: Will the matrix show my child's talents and future profession?
faq.a: The talent line suggests what is worth trying and what to look out for. A profession, a club or a school cannot be determined from a date: those come from the child's interests, their experience and your family.

faq.q: Are a child's destiny matrix and the parent-child line the same thing?
faq.a: No. A child's destiny matrix is either the child's whole chart or the parent–child compatibility chart. The parent-child line is three points inside any personal chart, A, O and J: the atmosphere of childhood, the attitude to children and the outer expression. Adults without children have one too.

faq.q: Is the matrix different for boys and girls?
faq.a: No. Sex plays no part in the calculation: a boy and a girl born on the same day have exactly the same chart.
